memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "And on the lampstand there were four cups shaped like almond flowers with buds and blossoms. One bud was under the first pair of branches extending from the lampstand, a second bud under the second pair, and a third bud under the third pair - six branches in all. The buds and the branches were all of one piece with the lampstand, hammered out of pure gold." - Exod 37:20-22 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The centre shaft carried more cups than any branch — four rather than three — and every pair of branches emerged from a bud on the central stem.

Everything came out of the middle. Nothing existed independently.

That structure quietly teaches what the New Testament states directly. Christ is the head, from whom the whole body, joined and held together, grows (Eph 4:15-16). He is before all things, and in Him all things hold together (Col 1:17).

Where does a church go wrong? Almost always the same way — something other than Christ moves to the centre. A personality, a programme, a tradition, a cause, even good doctrine held as an end in itself. The branches remain, but the centre has shifted.

The same happens in individual lives. Ministry can quietly replace the Master. Service can crowd out fellowship. Martha was busy with genuinely good work while Mary sat at Jesus' feet (Luke 10:41-42), and Jesus was clear about which mattered more.

Repeated three times in these verses is the phrase "of one piece." Not assembled. Grown from the same source.

Check your centre. Everything else in your life is meant to grow out of it.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What has quietly moved to the centre of your life?
2. Is your service flowing from your relationship with Christ, or replacing it?
3. What would it look like to put Him back at the centre this week?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord Jesus, be the centre of everything in my life. Let all my activity grow out of knowing You. Amen.
